title: A Unique Rare-Earth Cluster within a Calixarene Sandwich: Parallels in the Chemistry of Cyclosiloxanes and Calixarenes

material_class.structural_family: planar μ4-OH Nd4 cluster sandwiched between two fully deprotonated p-t-butyltetrathiacalix[4]arene ligands

synthesis.procedure: p-t-Butyltetrathiacalix[4]arene·CHCl3 (0.10 g, 0.12 mmol) was dissolved in dmf (1 ml) containing Et3N (0.15 ml) and mixed with [Nd(dmso)4(NO3)3] (0.18 g, 0.28 mmol) in dmf (0.5 ml). The pink-violet solution was left in a closed vessel for 2 months without depositing crystals. A layer of acetonitrile was then added and the solution was exposed to the atmosphere so that evaporation could occur; large violet crystals deposited slowly over a further 2 months. The residual solid was collected by filtration, washed with ethanol and dried in air.
synthesis.time: 2 months standing, then crystallization over a further 2 months
synthesis.vessel_or_method: closed vessel, then acetonitrile layer with atmospheric evaporation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Slow atmospheric evaporation after layering with acetonitrile gave violet crystals; the solid was filtered, washed with ethanol and dried in air.

properties.summary: SQUID susceptibility (5–300 K, 12 T) shows apparent Curie–Weiss behaviour. The room-temperature moment is 7.9 BM, similar to the related siloxane cluster and well below the 4×3.68 BM expected for four independent Nd(III) f3 ions. Nd···Nd separations are 3.6746(3) and 3.6888(3) Å; the extent of exchange versus other magnetic interactions is not established.

measurements.name: room-temperature magnetic moment
measurements.conditions: room temperature; SQUID, field 12 T, data range 5–300 K

source_locations.location: Magnetism section and Fig. 2; Structure Determination
